section_summary: This section opens with a Board of Economic Warfare letter enclosing corrections to earlier meeting minutes, minutes of its July 1 and July 15, 1943 meetings, and a revised report on Japan’s war economy. The meeting records address trade with Portugal and Sweden, approval of Board programs, and wooden vessel construction. The report, which continues beyond page 62, assesses Japan’s shipping, transport, raw materials, oil, steel, electric power, and consumer supplies.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting Board records
subfiles.about: Transmits a revised Japan war economy report, July meeting minutes, and proposed corrections to earlier minutes.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the revised report, July 1 and 15 minutes, and suggested changes to earlier minutes.

subfiles.title: Proposed correction to August 18, 1942 minutes
subfiles.about: Restates discussion of submitting a draft plan to the President.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies that the proposed step was presidential review of a draft plan.

subfiles.title: Proposed corrections to November 27, 1942 minutes
subfiles.about: Revises passages on food supply, Costa Rican production, and public health employment.
subfiles.summary: Corrects Rockefeller’s remarks on transport, Central American food production, and public health work.

subfiles.title: Proposed correction to December 17, 1942 minutes
subfiles.about: Restates Rockefeller’s question about Lend-Lease funding and supplies for Hispaniola and Puerto Rico.
subfiles.summary: Clarifies remarks about highway funding and criticism of Puerto Rican supply methods.

subfiles.title: Proposed corrections to December 31, 1942 minutes
subfiles.about: Restates Rockefeller’s remarks on Bolivian food statistics, production, and health programs.
subfiles.summary: Corrects passages concerning Bolivian food supplies, a health agreement, and balanced meals.

subfiles.title: Proposed correction to December 31, 1942 minutes
subfiles.about: Clarifies a remark about cash purchases of bauxite and mahogany.
subfiles.summary: Says cash purchases of bauxite and mahogany would be hard to explain publicly.

subfiles.title: Proposed addition to January 14, 1943 minutes
subfiles.about: Adds a statement on aid if gold mining closures cause unemployment in Colombia and Nicaragua.
subfiles.summary: Rockefeller offers cooperative programs if unavailable machinery and shipping force gold mining closures.

subfiles.title: Proposed correction to May 6, 1943 minutes
subfiles.from: R. P. Patterson and Adlai Stevenson
subfiles.about: Records differing views on continued negotiations and shipments to Sweden.
subfiles.summary: Qualifies apparent agreement on negotiations by recording Patterson’s, Knox’s, and White’s objections.

subfiles.title: Proposed correction to June 3, 1943 minutes
subfiles.about: Restates Rockefeller’s concerns about United States intervention in a Mexican monopoly agreement.
subfiles.summary: Rockefeller says replacing the Cyanamid proposal could offend Mexico and asks for a clear United States economic policy.

subfiles.title: Correction to June 17, 1943 minutes
subfiles.about: Corrects John Lockwood’s institutional affiliation in the attendance record.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Lockwood with the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs.

subfiles.title: Minutes of the Board of Economic Warfare meeting, July 1, 1943
subfiles.about: Records discussion of Portuguese tungsten and sardine trade and a proposed Swedish trade agreement.
subfiles.summary: Members consider whether to seek stronger concessions from Portugal after its agreement with Germany. They review proposed Swedish limits on exports, credits, and military transit in exchange for petroleum and basic rations. Several members question the value and enforceability of the Swedish concessions; their views are to be conveyed to the Secretary of State.

subfiles.title: Minutes of the Board of Economic Warfare meeting, July 15, 1943
subfiles.about: Records discussion of the Board’s appropriation amendment and the wooden vessel program.
subfiles.summary: Perkins explains a new requirement for written majority approval of general economic programs funded abroad and proposes policy resolutions. Rockefeller reports that improved shipping and long construction times favor ending further wooden vessel construction; the Board agrees.

subfiles.title: Amendment to the Board of Economic Warfare appropriation bill
subfiles.about: Sets a written majority approval requirement for certain expenditures abroad after August 15, 1943.
subfiles.summary: Requires approved general programs or policies to be filed with the Secretary of State before expenditure.

subfiles.title: Letter to Clarence Cannon on the proposed appropriation amendment
subfiles.from: Executive Director, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Warns that an ambiguously worded Senate amendment could require Board approval of individual operating decisions.
subfiles.summary: The executive director argues that narrow interpretation would make routine import, export, and analysis work impracticable and asks House conferees to revise the amendment.

subfiles.title: Notice to holders of EP 60
subfiles.about: Instructs holders to replace the original report text while retaining its maps and charts.
subfiles.summary: Destroy the original text; keep its maps and charts for the revised version.

subfiles.title: Japan’s War Economy — 1943
subfiles.from: Board of Economic Warfare, Enemy Branch
subfiles.about: Assesses Japan’s capacity to sustain and expand wartime production in 1943.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that shipping losses and limited processing capacity constrain Japan more than access to raw materials. Its pages in this section examine merchant shipping, rail links, oil and steel production, strategic minerals, electric power, and consumer supplies, using estimates and tables throughout. It describes Japan’s concentration of industry in an Inner Zone and its dependence on transport from occupied territories. The report continues beyond page 62.
